/pages/1/summary: Three service areas form the entry point: websites, agents and automations, and apps and portals. What matters is the task, your existing systems and a verifiable scope.
/pages/1/sections/0/body: Three service areas form the entry point: websites, agents and automations, and apps and portals. What matters is the task, your existing systems and a verifiable scope.
/pages/1/sections/1/heading: From the goal to the right service
/pages/1/sections/1/body: For a public presence with services and contact paths, you start with websites. For recurring enquiries, appointments, inboxes or draft quotes, you look at agents and automation. For protected project overviews, documents and separated team permissions, the entry point is apps and portals. Which parts belong together is clarified along the concrete user journey.
/pages/1/sections/2/heading: Adapt a building block or build a custom solution
/pages/1/sections/2/body: An existing building block can fit when mainly the brand, tone, rules and connections need to be adapted. A custom solution is appropriate when your data model or the interplay of several systems has to be newly developed. Reuse, adaptation limits, usage rights and operation are described separately in the quote; the existence of a reference is not yet a delivery commitment.
/pages/1/sections/3/heading: What is agreed in the end
/pages/1/sections/3/body: Before the build, we record the goal, scope and acceptance criteria. During implementation, a preview, open decisions and result reports are meant to make progress verifiable. Acceptance covers the agreed features and the handover of the related documents; any ongoing support scope is defined separately.
/pages/1/metadata/description: Three service areas form the entry point: websites, agents and automations, and apps and portals. What matters is the task, your existing systems and a verifiable scope.
/pages/2/summary: A website should explain services clearly and lead to the right enquiry. We clarify content, navigation, languages, contact path and maintenance before a concrete scope is set.
/pages/2/sections/0/body: A website should explain services clearly and lead to the right enquiry. We clarify content, navigation, languages, contact path and maintenance before a concrete scope is set.
/pages/2/sections/1/heading: From the offer to the right enquiry
/pages/2/sections/1/body: We structure which services your business explains, which questions visitors have and which contact path fits each case. From this we derive pages, navigation and the required language versions. A landing page focuses on a single offer; a company website connects several services. A shop adds product data, a cart and an ordering process and therefore needs its own scope.
/pages/2/sections/2/body: Before publishing, we check the agreed path from the entry page to the enquiry: content, links, mobile operation and understandable feedback when details are missing. Required texts, images and usage rights are clarified. A shown form draft is not yet a confirmed submission; real contact connections belong explicitly in the scope of services.
/pages/2/sections/3/body: For the handover we define who may change content, where the project is operated and which documents your team receives. For custom-built parts, code and data handover are agreed; for reused building blocks, the usage rights are named. Editorial maintenance, technical changes and ongoing support are separate services. Visibility or enquiry numbers are not guaranteed.
/pages/2/metadata/description: A website should explain services clearly and lead to the right enquiry. We clarify content, navigation, languages, contact path and maintenance before a concrete scope is set.

/pages/3/summary: We start with a concrete process: input, processing, exception and handover. Rules, access and approvals limit execution. Marketing tasks can first be prepared as a structured briefing.
/pages/3/sections/0/body: We start with a concrete process: input, processing, exception and handover. Rules, access and approvals limit execution. Marketing tasks can first be prepared as a structured briefing.
/pages/3/sections/1/body: The toolkit describes a chat agent for follow-up questions and handovers, appointment booking based on free calendar slots, email triage by topic and responsibility, and a quote generator for drafts. A knowledge agent is meant to use approved documents with source references. We choose one bounded use case; listing these building blocks does not mean they are all already connected to your system.
/pages/3/sections/2/heading: Define access and approvals up front
/pages/3/sections/2/body: Calendar, inbox and other business systems are connected via suitable interfaces, as far as the respective provider allows. We separate reading, drafting and executing. You decide when a human must decide, for example before sending, binding quotes or changes. Missing details and uncertain results lead to a follow-up question instead of an invented commitment.
/pages/3/sections/3/heading: Test a process and measure it
/pages/3/sections/3/body: For the pilot we choose a measurable goal, for example the time to first response. In the preview we check the normal case, missing data, blocked actions and the handover to a human. After approved go-live, the same metric is measured again. The comparison shows the actual course; it is not a pre-promised time saving or revenue.
/pages/3/metadata/description: We start with a concrete process: input, processing, exception and handover. Rules, access and approvals limit execution. Marketing tasks can first be prepared as a structured briefing.

/pages/4/summary: Customer and internal processes need clear roles, data areas and states. Together we clarify who may see which information and which steps they may perform.
/pages/4/sections/0/body: Customer and internal processes need clear roles, data areas and states. Together we clarify who may see which information and which steps they may perform.
/pages/4/sections/1/heading: Bring quote, project and documents together
/pages/4/sections/1/body: A customer portal can connect quotes with version and status, project progress, acceptances, documents and invoice overviews. For internal work, responsibilities, open decisions and reports are added. We select the required views and actions; viewing an invoice, accepting an order and triggering a payment are different functions.
/pages/4/sections/2/heading: Each role sees its own area
/pages/4/sections/2/body: For customers, team members and partners, we clarify which data they see and which steps they may perform. Signing in alone grants no rights to other projects or internal administration. Invitations, tenant assignment and sensitive changes require appropriate permissions. These rules are checked at every affected process, not only at the menu display.
/pages/4/sections/3/body: For a quote we distinguish draft, approved version, acceptance, rejection and change request. For further processes we likewise define what is shown during loading, empty data, errors and blocked actions. Connections to existing systems, document downloads and notifications are agreed individually and tested in a preview. Prepared sample data stays recognizable as such.
/pages/4/metadata/description: Customer and internal processes need clear roles, data areas and states. Together we clarify who may see which information and which steps they may perform.

/pages/10/summary: NeXify builds websites, apps and AI-supported processes for businesses. The focus is on Germany. The confirmed company details of NeXify AI FACTORY B.V. remain authoritative for provider information.
/pages/10/sections/0/body: NeXify builds websites, apps and AI-supported processes for businesses. The focus is on Germany. The confirmed company details of NeXify AI FACTORY B.V. remain authoritative for provider information.
/pages/10/sections/1/body: NeXify AI combines consulting, development and operation into tangible results for small and medium-sized businesses. The guiding principle “Chat it. Automate it.” stands for a clear path: describe what is needed – and reliably automate recurring work. The focus is on the European market with a German- and Dutch-speaking emphasis.
/pages/10/sections/2/body: We define the goal, scope and acceptance criteria in advance and make progress visible through a preview, open decisions and result reports. Claims are substantiated, open points are named openly. A reference is not yet a delivery commitment, and a draft quote stays non-binding until separately approved.
/pages/10/sections/3/body: The operator is NeXify AI FACTORY B.V., with its registered office in the Netherlands. Market preference changes nothing about registration, tax or provider identity. Provider information, data protection and contractual bases are collected in the Law and Transparency area.
/pages/10/metadata/description: NeXify AI FACTORY B.V. is the named company context. The focus on German users does not change any Dutch provider or registration data. Binding company data is taken exclusively from the verified provider profile.
/pages/11/summary: Describe your project: a website, a simpler process or a shared workspace. You can prepare your request in the project assistant or reach Pascal directly by email.
/pages/11/sections/0/body: Describe your project: a website, a simpler process or a shared workspace. You can prepare your request in the project assistant or reach Pascal directly by email.
/pages/11/sections/1/body: Describe your goal in a few sentences and name which systems are affected. You receive an assessment and, where useful, a next step. A first conversation or a draft quote is non-binding and only becomes the basis for cooperation with separate approval.
/pages/11/sections/2/body: We sort out need and scope, record acceptance criteria and outline a possible path. Nothing is promised unchecked. There are no invented cities, workshops or references – only what is actually stored and approved is shown.
/pages/11/sections/3/body: We use your information solely to process your request. No access credentials or secrets are requested via this form. Details on data use can be found in the data protection area.
